scope: spend control process
evidence: Service Manual (updated 2026-04-01): "Digital and technology spend controls were replaced on 1 April 2026. From this date, central government departments are responsible for making most of their own digital and technology spending decisions." TCoP (updated 2025-07-07) still says: "You must consider all points of the TCoP as part of the Cabinet Office spend control process."
guidance: Treat the Service Manual as current on who approves digital spend. TCoP remains current on the technology standards themselves, only its spend control section is stale.

guidance: Check current thresholds in the Service Manual before relying on the £10m figure.

scope: who assures TCoP compliance and approves digital and technology spend
evidence: DDaT Playbook (2023), DDaT assurance: "Compliance with this code is assured through the Cabinet Office spend control process". Service Manual (updated 2026-04-01): "Digital and technology spend controls were replaced on 1 April 2026."
guidance: Treat the Service Manual as current on who approves digital and technology spend. The rest of the playbook, including its separate commercial spend control, is not affected by this.

scope: technology spend control sign-off before going live
evidence: Gate 4 workbook (republished 2026-08-20), 4.2: "Cabinet Office (CO) controls have been sighted on the FBC and the project has satisfied the CO controls teams commercial and technology spend control requirements." Service Manual (updated 2026-04-01): "Digital and technology spend controls were replaced on 1 April 2026."
guidance: The two disagree on technology spend control; this library cannot say which is right. Check with NISTA or the department's digital spend approvers. The commercial spend control in the same sentence is a separate control.
